newsitem.title: USA: Amoco estimates NDC production at Alabama facility.
newsitem.headline: Amoco estimates NDC production at Alabama facility.

text.p: Amoco Corp said Wednesday it expects to reach a production rate of 27,000 tons per year of dimethyl-2,6-naphthalene dicarboxylate (NDC), a chemical used to make film for video and data storage tapes by early 1998 at its Decatur, Ala. facility
Amoco said it began commercial production of the chemical at its Decatur facility on April 1, 1997.

NDC is a raw material used in the packaging, film, fiber and engineering resin markets, both to modify existing polyesters and in a new polyester, polyethylene naphthalate (PEN). Commercial products based on NDC include film for the photographic industry's Advanced Photo System, as well as video and data storage tapes.

Starting April 1, 1997, Amoco said it expects to be able to supply existing contract customers, but does not expect to be able to accept new business above its current contracts until additional capacity is built.
Amoco said it is studying longer-term NDC supply options, including increasing the production efficiency of the Decatur NDC plant and a new NDC complex.
Amoco produces and markets oil, natural gas and petrochemicals.
